newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures extend losses by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures extend losses by close.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures extended losses in the afternoon to end Thursday at session lows but industry buying on the dips helped slow the fall.
Trade houses were again seen as the main sellers as origins shied away amid sliding prices. Traders said the latest fall in New York arabica futures had a limited effect.
"London didn't really react," said one trader. "It's a sign of the times that they are two different markets."
By the close, May stood at the day's low of $1,610 a tonne, down $31 on the day. That level was seen as immediate support on the charts.
New York arabicas took a tumble on profit-taking following Wednesday's rise to a contract high, basis May.
Traders said rumours of a sharp increase in U.S. coffee stocks and news of a poor Brazilian coffee auction sale weighed on sentiment.

So far, the market showed little reaction to news a strike by stevedores continued to halt loadings at Brazil's key Santos port as coffee volume coming out from Brazil is not substantial at this time of the year.

The strike, which paralysed most loading operations except for a few vessels including one loading orange juice, is expected to continue through Saturday. It is set to spread to the national level on Friday.
In view of the absence of other market-moving factors, the London market looked set to hold at the current $1,610-$1,675 band after recovering from a one-month low of $1,515 last week.
But it could face an uphill struggle to revisit the $1,700 or even the $1,800 levels seen in early March at the height of this year's rally.
